instructions: Put a large pot of water on to boil over high heat.
Meanwhile, thinly slice the onion. Cut the core out of the cabbage and cut a quarter of the head into 1 inch squares. Peel the carrot and cut it into thin 2 inch matchsticks.
Pull the stems off the 4 shiitake and slice the caps. Cut 4 of the scallions into 2 inch pieces.
In a small bowl, stir together 1/4 cup soy sauce, 2 tbsp sake, 2 tsp mirin and 1 tsp dashi powder.
If the 1 lb shrimp aren't peeled, peel and devein them. Pat them dry with paper towels and toss them with the 1/4 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper.
Drop 4 of the udon blocks into the boiling water for 30 to 40 seconds, just until the noodles loosen apart. Drain them well.

Heat your largest frying pan or a wok over medium high and add 1 tbsp of the oil. Lay the shrimp in a single layer and cook for about 1 minute, until the undersides turn pink. Flip them and cook the other side for about 1 minute, until they're opaque all the way through. Move them to a plate.
Add the other 1 tbsp oil and the onion to the pan. Stir fry until it's soft, about 2 minutes.
Add the cabbage, carrot, shiitake and scallions and toss them in the oil. Cover the pan, turn the heat to medium low and steam them for 3 minutes, until the cabbage has just wilted.
Turn the heat back up to medium high. Add the udon and toss it gently with tongs so the noodles don't break.

Pour the sauce down the hot side of the pan and let it sizzle for a few seconds, then toss everything until the noodles are evenly brown. Put the shrimp back in and toss for about 1 minute to heat them through. If there's still liquid in the pan, keep tossing over the heat until it's gone.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve topped with the 6 tbsp bonito flakes, with the 1/4 cup pickled red ginger on the side.
method_notes: Both read versions blanch frozen udon briefly, stir fry onion, carrot, cabbage and mushrooms, then toss the noodles with a soy based sauce until it's absorbed. Just One Cookbook (the lead) cooks its protein first in the pan, steams the vegetables under a lid for 3 minutes and seasons with soy, sake, mirin and dashi powder, then tops it with bonito flakes and pickled red ginger. It names seafood as a swap for its pork belly. Two Plaid Aprons sears the shrimp separately and adds them back at the end, uses a soy, oyster sauce, Worcestershire and sugar sauce and scrambles an egg in. This one follows the lead's sauce and steaming, with the shrimp seared and set aside so they don't overcook.
